description.narrative:
Overall objective: To stimulate inclusive sustainable economic growth with a special focus on energy efficiency (EE) appliances and industrial processes.
Expected outcomes:
Outcome 1: The uptake of Energy Efficient Appliances in Zambia has increased through national policy and capacity-building interventions as well as private sector development, linked to the regional EELA project.
The objective is to increase the adoption of energy efficient appliances in Zambia, thereby reducing poverty and mitigating adverse environmental impacts. The project will contribute to improve the policy and regulatory framework, strengthen capacity, and enhance private sector investments, particularly focusing on the development of the energy service companies' (ESCOs) market and local value chains.
Outcome 2: A private sector Industry Clean Tech Platform (ICTP) is set up to accelerate investments in the low-carbon transformation of the industrial sector targeting high impact industries.
The objective is to set up a platform for identifying and promoting clean technology solutions within the industrial sector, focusing on the agriculture value chain. The ICTP aims to stimulate economic growth, job creation, and environmental sustainability by supporting industries in introducing energy management systems and facilitating access to suitable technology and financing opportunities. The high impact agricultural value chain industries that will act as champions will be identified during the inception phase.*
Outcome 3: Skills for repair, maintenance and end-of-life treatment of energy efficient equipment are enhanced in Zambia with a special focus on e-waste management.
The aim is to enhance skills for the repair, maintenance, and end-of-life treatment of energy-efficient equipment in Zambia contributing to e-waste management including rural off-grid technologies like solar home systems, off-grid refrigerators, and off-grid productive use equipment (PUE) systems. This will be achieved through a comprehensive market and feasibility report, policy advice, and targeted capacity building and collaboration with public and private partners on the provision of demand-driven and future skills through Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET).

EELA Zambia-projektet (Energy Efficiency for Sustainable Livelihoods in Africa - Zambia) bygger på det regionala EELA-program som är på väg att gå in i sin andra fas av genomförnade. Liknande projekt genomförs samtidigt i Kenya och Zimbabwe. Det övergripande målet för det fyraåriga projektet (2025-2028) är att stimulera inkluderande hållbar ekonomisk tillväxt med särskilt fokus på energieffektiv utrustning och industriella processer. De tre huvudsakliga förväntade resultaten är (i) Användningen av energieffektiv utrustning i Zambia har ökat genom insatser för nationella policyer och kapacitetsuppbyggnad samt utveckling av den privata sektorn, kopplat till det regionala EELA-programmet; (ii) Etablerandet av en industriell clean tech­plattform (ICTP) för den privata sektorn med målet att främja investeringar i industrins koldioxidneutrala omställning; och (iii) Förbättrade kunskaper och färdigheter för reparation, underhåll och hantering av uttjänt energieffektiv utrustning i Zambia, med särskilt fokus på hantering av el- avfall.

The EELA Zambia project (Energy Efficiency for Sustainable Livelihoods in Africa - Zambia) builds on the regional EELA programme which is about to enter its second phase of implementation. Similar projects are simultaneously being implemented in Kenya and Zimbabwe. The overall objective of the four-year project (2025-2028) is to stimulate inclusive sustainable economic growth with a special focus on energy efficiency appliances and industrial processes. The three main expected outcomes are (i) The uptake of energy efficient appliances in Zambia has increased through national policy and capacity building interventions as well as private sector development, linked to the regional EELA programme; (ii) A private sector Industry Clean Tech Platform (ICTP) is set up to accelerate investments in the low carbon transformation of the industrial sector targeting high impact industries; and (iii) Skills for repair, maintenance and end-of-life treatment of energy efficient equipment are enhanced in Zambia, with a special focus on e-waste management.
